<section class="term-panel term-method"><h2>What this research can support</h2><p>The fitted yield is decomposed into risk-neutral yield and term premium in the Adrian–Crump–Moench model. These are model-implied zero-coupon estimates, distinct from Treasury constant-maturity par yields. Reconciliation is an arithmetic check, not proof of a causal explanation.</p>
<p>Daily and monthly series, different maturities and the three components share one fitted model. They are not independent signals. The retained workbook is one acquired vintage: historical values may have been revised, and this history is not a point-in-time backtest.</p>
<p>Source observation dates, acquisition time and publication time are separate. Daily observations have a seven-calendar-day ceiling, monthly observations a 70-day ceiling; acquisitions expire after 26 hours. Release-calendar validation remains unavailable. A failed acquisition or regressed source withholds current readings.</p>
<p><strong>Portfolio consequence: unavailable.</strong> These measurements have no qualified forecast, Calls vote, target weight or execution permission. WAIT means abstain. Decisions require independently tested evidence and portfolio-specific risk inputs.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/data_indicators/term-premia-tabs">NY Fed dataset and model</a> · <a href="https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2014/05/treasury-term-premia-1961-present/">Official methodology</a> · <a href="/data/term-premium.json?exact=1&nogen=1">Current research packet</a></p></section>
